attributes.name: Reprocessing as a Service (RaaS)
attributes.description:
Reprocessing as a Service (RaaS) — an orchestration microservice platform deployed into EKS under ADP.next, providing managed reprocessing capabilities consumed by the KPI framework pipeline and supporting RPU reprocessing steps within KPI jobs.
  - Jointly developed by BMW Planck and CTW Turing/Gosling teams; encompasses product ownership, engineering, development, DevOps, and UX/UI functions; managed as part of the RaaS/RDQ/KPI-FW cluster
  - Facilitates configuration, submission, and management of reprocessing jobs; performs full orchestration, verification, and validation of user jobs for reprocessing previously collected driving data with more recent sensor or AD software versions
  - Feeds raw sensor and vehicle bus data to RPUs; orchestrates, mounts, and collects RPU data without transforming or modifying it
  - Hosts ADMake RPU availability and the Quality Stage, which rejects DQ-flagged intervals; triggers reprocessing jobs for candidates
  - When Data Quality Checks are enabled, communicates with RDQ to verify session data suitability before proceeding; can reject reprocessing for a session if data quality checks fail
  - Deployed in the same Realm as RDQ and is usually deployed together with it
  - Supports session interval configuration with two modes for determining the reprocessing interval; implements output caching for efficiency
  - Follows cloud-native, schema-per-service, and orchestration-first design principles
  - Receives ongoing updates including new features, bug fixes, and API changes; subject to downtime notifications per the downtime communication list
  - Documented in the BMW Group Confluence RaaS space and the comprehensive onboarding reference documentation; support contactable via Microsoft Teams channel: ADP.next | [RPR] Reprocessing as a Service support

attributes.name: RaaS Platform
attributes.description:
RaaS Platform refers to two distinct platforms sharing the acronym:

1. **Reprocessing as a Service** — BMW's cloud-based platform for re-processing previously collected driving data with updated sensor or AD software versions, orchestrating the full lifecycle: configuration, submission, scheduling, execution, data-quality validation, and output delivery.

2. **Rendering as a Service** — a platform providing rendering capabilities through a microservices/service-oriented architecture running on Amazon EKS, where each microservice is independently deployable and owns its data.
  - Foundational shared resources are provided by the `raas-realm-infra` component.
  - Follows a continuous delivery model with explicitly numbered, cross-repository releases.

attributes.name: RPU
attributes.description:
Reprocessing Unit (RPU) — containerised atomic execution unit within RaaS that ingests raw sensor and vehicle bus data from original recordings and reprocesses it using updated sensor or AD software versions to produce derived data.
  - RaaS schedules, mounts, and collects data from RPUs but never transforms it
  - Multiple RPU types are available and enumerable via GET /v1/rpus, which also supports version validity queries
  - Configured in the job payload via rpus[].rpuType and rpus[].softwareVersion fields
  - Receives converted vehicle bus data from the Boardnet Converter; requires data in a serialisation format compatible with its algorithms
  - RPUs replicate physical vehicle sensor setups and are orchestrated in a dependency graph representing vehicle sensor dependencies | Rendering Processing Unit (RPU) within RaaS, validated by RCC containers and generating variable S3 storage footprints.
  - Fails with exit code 12 within 7–9 seconds when no repro trigger signal or MIPI input stream is present
  - Which RPU generates the most S3 data is an open requirement

attributes.name: Job Service
attributes.description:
Microservice owning the `job` / `job_service` schema in the shared Aurora cluster. Serves as the single entry point (API gateway) for all external interactions with RaaS and all reprocessing operations, exposing an OpenAPI-documented REST API with endpoints `/health`, `/jobs`, and `/jobs/{job_id}` for creating, retrieving, and deleting KPI jobs.
  - Key Aurora tables: `jobs`, `job_status`, `job_results`
  - Handles full job lifecycle: accepts job creation requests, validates inputs (including pre-flight data quality checks), persists job metadata, and exposes status endpoints
  - Publishes job-created events to SQS for downstream consumption by the Job Scheduler, which dispatches to Argo Workflows
  - Manages asynchronous DQ integration: produces `dq-request` messages, consumes `dq-response` results, and determines which intervals are valid for reprocessing submission
  - Consumes job-completed results and emits events on all job state transitions

attributes.name: Job Scheduler
attributes.description:
RaaS microservice responsible for receiving submitted jobs from the Job Service (via SQS `job.created` / job-scheduler-intake queue), queuing them by priority, and dispatching them to Argo Workflows for execution (emitting `job.scheduled` events with a `workflow_id`).
  - Owns the `job_scheduler` / `scheduler` schema; key tables: `dispatch_log`, `priority_queue`
  - Processes the queue at a fixed rate of ~4 jobs per 20 seconds, up to a maximum of ~2,800 concurrent running jobs on Argo
  - Re-queues evicted jobs when a CRITICAL priority job preempts them
  - Queries the RPU Metadata Service to resolve the correct RPU image for each job
  - Operates independently per environment (DEV, INT, PROD)

attributes.name: Data Quality Service
attributes.description:
Microservice within the RaaS platform responsible for pre-flight and on-demand validation of input data assets across RaaS pipelines. Owns the `data_quality` / `dq` schema; key tables: `dq_checks`, `stream_inventory`.
  - Validates that raw sensor data in S3 contains streams required by the RPU for a requested time interval; checks cover stream existence, temporal coverage, completeness, freshness, and integrity
  - Consumes `dq-request` messages and produces `dq-response` results (async); also called synchronously via REST by the Job Service for pre-flight checks before job execution begins
  - Applies validation rules and enforces quality thresholds across RaaS pipelines
  - Consumed by realms: RaaSv1, LLP, GeminiAVP, E2EDataTracing, BMWRpuSandbox
  - DEV: https://raas-dq-dev.api.aws.orionadp.com/ — Keycloak client `orion-178345759618-raas-dq-dev`
  - INT: https://raas-dq-int.api.aws.orionadp.com/ — Keycloak client `orion-361298712206-raas-dq-int`
  - PROD: https://raas-dq.api.aws.orionadp.com/ — Keycloak client `orion-984792474975-raas-dq`

attributes.name: RPU Metadata Service
attributes.description:
Central registry microservice owning the `rpu` schema (also referenced as `rpu_metadata`) for all Reprocessing Unit (RPU) information. Manages RPU type definitions, version records, container images (URIs, tags, build metadata), stream definitions, and resource profiles. attributes.name: Reprocessing Job
attributes.description:
A discrete unit of reprocessing work submitted to the RaaS platform (via the `submitJob` endpoint), representing the re-execution of previously collected driving data with updated sensor or autonomous driving function software versions.
  - Identified by a unique `job_id` (e.g., `6b3bd78e-7505-489f-a62a-75ecc7c6659b`) and associated with an `rpu_type`, `session_id`, and priority level
  - Maps one-to-one to an Argo Workflow resource, executed on a node within the platform
  - Transitions through defined states (e.g., `SUBMITTED`) and includes verification and validation steps orchestrated by RaaS
  - When Data Quality Checks are enabled, the job invokes RDQ verification before proceeding
  - Costs are attributed to the customer function that owns the job | A discrete unit of work submitted to the RaaS platform via the job submission API, tracked by a returned jobId, referencing a recorded driving session and one or more RPUs for reprocessing.
  - Configured with parameters: session, RPU type, software version, project name, context ID, priority, and optional time interval (loggerStartTime, loggerEndTime)
  - Acceptance is conditional on passing a Data Quality check against the associated session, unless disableQualityCheck is set to true
  - Contains tasks that inherit the job's priority

attributes.name: RDQ (Reprocessing Data Quality)
attributes.description:
RDQ (Reprocessing Data Quality) is a platform service providing data quality oversight, validation, and session tracking for ingested data relevant to customer function development (e.g. AEB, ASF).
  - Analyses reprocessability and KPI-computability of ingested sessions and intervals; triggers and evaluates reprocessing candidate runs
  - Assesses session data quality for specified RPUs by evaluating DQ Tags and returning a boolean (true/false) indicating whether a session is safe to reprocess; communicates with RaaS for this determination
  - Exposes the RDQ API for configuring check relevance and mapping DQ checks to RPUs
  - Backs session details dashboards and data analysis workflows via interaction with the Postgres RDQ database
  - Supports two authentication mechanisms: Keycloak (JWT) for human/browser access and IAM (SigV4) for machine-to-machine access

attributes.name: DQ Tags

attributes.name: Interval Table
attributes.description:
Relational database table representing time intervals managed by the Scenario Classifier, keyed by session_id, interval_start_unix_ns, and interval_end_unix_ns. Populated periodically via Data Search query execution and serves as input for Session Flow.
  - Each interval is an atomic unit of data defined by its session_id + start_ns + end_ns composite key — fully usable or not; no partial qualification applies
  - Each interval represents a job ramification, with columns including: interval_id (PK), task_id (PK, TEXT), type (TEXT, NOT NULL), job_id (FK/TEXT, NOT NULL), session_id (TEXT, NOT NULL), logger_start_time, logger_end_time, status (ENUM, NOT NULL), start_time, end_time, duration_seconds (default 0), error_message (TEXT, default ''), input (TEXT, default ''), output (TEXT, default ''), created_at, updated_at

attributes.name: Reprocessing Data Quality & Session Flow (RDQ)

  - Assessed as having no safety impact but potential cost impact

  - RDQ variant specifically manages interval extraction

attributes.name: Data Quality Check
attributes.description:
Data quality validations performed on a session to ensure recorded data is accurate and reliable. Conducted across ECU components. Results are DQ Tags identifying intervals where issues were detected or not. Approximately 500-600 different checks exist across three source groups, generating thousands of DQ Tags per session (commonly >10,000 per session). | Data quality validation component within the RDQ (Rendering Data Quality) framework, operating as part of the RaaS reprocessing pipeline. Evaluates data quality across pipelines and data assets, with checks scoped per customer function — each function has its own applicable set of DQ checks.
  - For a job to be accepted, all applicable checks must exist (Checked Status) and be green within the selected interval
  - Evaluates stream availability and data quality of ingested sessions and scenario intervals to determine reprocessability and KPI-computability
  - Developer documentation and configuration details are maintained in the `reprocessing-data-quality` subfolder README

descriptionSegments.text: Data quality validations performed on a session to ensure recorded data is accurate and reliable. Conducted across ECU components. Results are DQ Tags identifying intervals where issues were detected or not. Approximately 500-600 different checks exist across three source groups, generating thousands of DQ Tags per session (commonly >10,000 per session).
Validation process within the RDQ system responsible for checking data quality across pipelines and data assets.
A set of Data Quality checks relevant to each customer function within the RDQ (Rendering Data Quality) framework. Each customer function has its own set of applicable DQ checks.
Data quality validation component in RaaS. Checks must all exist (Checked Status) and all be green in the selected interval for a job to be accepted.
Validation step within RDQ that evaluates stream availability and data quality of ingested sessions and scenario intervals to determine reprocessability and KPI-computability.
A data quality check component within the RaaS reprocessing pipeline. Developer documentation and configuration details are maintained in the reprocessing-data-quality subfolder README.
